# ADR-05: Route Unclassified Work Through a Dispatcher Agent

- Status: Proposed
- Decision Date: 2026-07-11

## Decision Timestamp

Date: 2026-07-11
Repository State: `58ea76a`
Related Task: Create a general task dispatcher
Known Constraints At This Time: Existing specialist agents retain their own contracts; missing capabilities are created through AgentSetupAgent.

## Decision Trigger

Users may not know which specialist agent owns a request. Direct selection exposes the full agent taxonomy and provides no defined path when no suitable agent exists.

## Architecture Significance

Affected Areas: Agent orchestration boundary and dependency direction.
Why This Decision Is Architecturally Significant: It introduces a routing layer between user intent and specialist execution.

## Decision Inputs

| Input | Classification | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| TaskDispatcherAgent was added | FACT | `58ea76a` |
| AgentSetupAgent is the capability-creation fallback | CONSTRAINT | Session request and `58ea76a` |
| Routing accuracy is adequate | UNKNOWN | No routing evaluation exists |

## Assumptions

- Specialist responsibility descriptions are sufficient for deterministic routing.

## Unknowns

- Ambiguity and misrouting rate.

## Options

1. Central dispatcher selects a specialist and escalates missing capabilities to AgentSetupAgent.
2. Users select specialists directly.
3. Every agent independently delegates when out of scope.

## Decision Matrix

| Criterion | Weight | Dispatcher | Direct | Distributed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Discoverability | 5 | 5 | 2 | 3 |
| Routing consistency | 5 | 4 | 2 | 1 |
| Coupling | 3 | 2 | 5 | 2 |

## Decision

Propose Option 1. The dispatcher owns classification and handoff, not domain execution. When no existing role fits, its routing outcome is escalation to AgentSetupAgent, followed by delegation to the created role.

## Why Not

### Why Not Option 2
Rejected Because: It preserves the original selection burden. Evidence: User's stated trigger. Trade-off We Avoided: Taxonomy knowledge requirement. Trade-off We Accepted Instead: Central routing dependency.

### Why Not Option 3
Rejected Because: Routing policy would be duplicated across every agent. Evidence: Existing specialist files have separate contracts. Trade-off We Avoided: Distributed drift. Trade-off We Accepted Instead: Dispatcher bottleneck.

## Adversarial Review

### Strongest Argument Against Recommended Option
The dispatcher becomes a single point of misclassification.
### Failure Scenario
It creates a new agent although an existing specialist was sufficient.
### Hidden Cost
Every agent addition requires taxonomy updates.
### Assumption Most Likely to Be Wrong
Role descriptions are mutually distinguishable.
### Condition Where Another Option Becomes Better
Direct selection is better for expert callers with stable agent names.

## Reversibility

Classification: HIGH
Rollback Method: Invoke specialists directly.
Migration Cost: Caller instruction changes.
Data Migration Required: No.
Downtime Risk: None.
Lock-in: Dispatcher naming and taxonomy.

## Reconsideration Triggers

- Two confirmed misroutes occur for the same responsibility boundary.
- Dispatcher updates become the dominant cost of adding agents.

## Implementation Verification

### Assumptions Verified
The dispatcher contract exists at `58ea76a`.
### Assumptions Invalidated
None evidenced.
### Unexpected Findings
No runtime routing evidence is stored.
### Decision Still Valid
UNKNOWN

## Independent Review

### Findings
Fallback creation could be independently changed, but it is modeled here as one outcome of the single routing decision, not as a separate agent-construction decision.
### ADR Changes Required
Resolved by limiting the decision to ownership of routing.
### Recommendation Challenged
YES

## Timeline and Contradictions

Implemented before strict ADR at `58ea76a`. No Accepted ADR contradiction was found.
